text:
Direct precedent: Klenitskiy & Vasilev’s *Turning Dross Into Gold Loss* (RecSys 2023) compares SASRec’s original one-negative BCE with full-catalog cross-entropy and sampled softmax using many negatives. SASRec becomes substantially stronger with these training changes, challenging architectural explanations for BERT4Rec’s advantage. Their sampled-softmax implementation shares a sampled negative set across timesteps within each user sequence; this sampling granularity is another control to preserve. These results support investigating objective and negative count, but do not establish that objective alone explains gains. [Paper and author implementation](https://github.com/antklen/sasrec-bert4rec-recsys23).

Petrov & Macdonald’s *gSASRec* (RecSys 2023) explicitly studies negative sampling and overconfidence, introducing generalized BCE and increasing negative counts. It also includes uniformly sampled softmax as a baseline, making it particularly relevant for comparing BCE-family objectives against sampled softmax. Its findings support treating negative count and probability calibration as separate experimental factors. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192).

Recommended controls, inferred from these precedents: cross objective × negative count while keeping architecture, sampled item IDs, sampling exclusions/granularity, valid training positions, initialization, batches and evaluation candidates fixed. Specify BCE reduction algebraically: positive loss plus mean negative loss preserves positive/negative group weights; averaging all K+1 terms changes those weights as K increases. Summing negatives changes them again. Match valid-position averaging and explicitly control regularization relative to data-loss scale. Start with temperature=1; tune temperature separately because it changes gradients and score scale. Compare equal-update and equal-compute budgets. The identified sources do not establish a single controlled study isolating objective, negative count, reduction, temperature and regularization simultaneously.
